title: Email Templates vs Campaigns
learningGoal: Understand the difference between email templates, campaigns, and workflow emails in LeadProspectrr.

items.title: Email Template
items.description: A reusable saved email like 'Thanks for booking a call' that you can use again and again

items.title: Email Campaign
items.description: A message sent to a group, like a monthly newsletter to your contact list

items.title: Workflow Email
items.description: An email sent automatically after a trigger, like when someone fills out a form

items.title: Template = the message
items.description: The actual email content you write and save

items.title: Campaign = who gets it and when
items.description: How you send that message to the right people at the right time

keyPoint: Start with templates first. Learn to write and save a good email template before using campaigns and workflows.

actionSteps.title: Review your current emails
actionSteps.description: Think about emails you send repeatedly to leads or clients

actionSteps.title: Identify template opportunities
actionSteps.description: List 3 emails you write often that could become templates

actionSteps.title: Navigate to Marketing > Emails
actionSteps.description: Familiarize yourself with where templates and campaigns live in LeadProspectrr

quizzes.question: What is the main difference between an email template and an email campaign?

options.option_text: Templates are more expensive than campaigns
A template is the reusable message; a campaign is who gets it and when it is sent
Campaigns can only be sent once
Templates are only for automated emails

quizzes.explanation: Templates are reusable email messages you create once and use multiple times. Campaigns are how you send those messages to specific groups of contacts.

quizzes.question: Which of these is an example of a workflow email?

options.option_text: A monthly newsletter you send to your entire list
A thank-you email template you save for future use
An email that sends automatically when someone fills out a form on your website
A one-time announcement about a new product

quizzes.explanation: Workflow emails are automated and triggered by specific actions, like filling out a form, booking an appointment, or making a purchase.

quizzes.question: What should you learn first before creating campaigns and workflows?

options.option_text: How to write complex automation rules
How to import contacts from a spreadsheet
How to create and save a good email template
How to design custom HTML emails

quizzes.explanation: Start with templates first. Once you know how to write effective email templates, you can use them in campaigns and workflows.

title: Plan Your Email Before Building
learningGoal: Learn how to plan your email by answering five key questions before creating it in LeadProspectrr.

items.title: Who is this email for?
items.description: Define your specific audience - new leads, past clients, webinar attendees

items.title: Why are they receiving it?
items.description: What triggered this email? What is the context?

items.title: What do I want them to do?
items.description: One clear action - book a call, download a guide, reply to the email

items.title: What link or button do they need?
items.description: The specific URL or call-to-action button they'll click

items.title: Should this be a reusable template?
items.description: Will you send this same type of email multiple times?

items.title: Coach following up on a free guide download
items.description: Goal: Thank them, give them the resource, and invite them to book a call - not tell their whole life story

keyPoint: One email. One message. One action. If your email tries to do too many things, people will do nothing.

actionSteps.title: Choose one email to write
actionSteps.description: Pick a specific email you need to create from your plan

actionSteps.title: Answer the five questions
actionSteps.description: Write down answers to who, why, what action, what link, and whether to save as template

actionSteps.title: Write one sentence for the goal
actionSteps.description: Summarize what this email needs to accomplish in a single sentence

quizzes.question: Why is it important to answer 'Who is this email for?' before writing?

options.option_text: So you can charge them more money
To know which font size to use
So you can tailor the message to their specific situation and needs
To decide what time to send it

quizzes.explanation: Knowing your audience helps you write relevant content that speaks to their specific situation, increasing the chances they'll take action.

quizzes.question: What happens if your email has too many ideas or calls-to-action?

options.option_text: People will share it more often
People will do nothing because they are confused about what to do
It will automatically be split into multiple emails
The email will be marked as spam

quizzes.explanation: When you give people too many options or messages, they experience decision paralysis and often take no action at all.

quizzes.question: When should you save an email as a reusable template?

options.option_text: Only for welcome emails
When you will send the same type of email multiple times
Only for emails with images
Never - templates are not recommended

quizzes.explanation: Save any email as a template if you'll send similar messages repeatedly - follow-ups, thank-yous, reminders, resource deliveries, etc.

title: Create an Email Template
learningGoal: Learn how to create a reusable email template in LeadProspectrr from start to finish.

items.title: 1. Go to Marketing > Emails > Templates
items.description: Navigate to the Templates section in LeadProspectrr

items.title: 2. Click New Template
items.description: Choose a blank template or simple layout to start

items.title: 3. Add a clear template name
items.description: Use descriptive names like 'Welcome - New Lead' or 'Follow-Up - No Response'

items.title: 4. Add subject line and email body
items.description: Write your message following the one email, one message, one action rule

items.title: 5. Add buttons or links
items.description: Include your call-to-action with working links

items.title: 6. Preview and test
items.description: Send yourself a test email to see how it looks

items.title: 7. Save the template
items.description: Your template is now ready to use in campaigns

items.title: Clear names make templates easy to find
items.description: Welcome - New Lead | Follow-Up - No Response | Thank You - After Session | Reminder - Upcoming Appointment | Offer - Book a Strategy Call | Resource Delivery - Free Guide

keyPoint: Always send yourself a test email before saving. Check how it looks on desktop and mobile.

actionSteps.title: Navigate to Marketing > Emails > Templates
actionSteps.description: Find the Templates section in your LeadProspectrr account

actionSteps.title: Create a new template
actionSteps.description: Click New Template and choose a simple layout

actionSteps.title: Name your template clearly
actionSteps.description: Use a descriptive name you'll recognize later

actionSteps.title: Send a test email
actionSteps.description: Preview and send a test to yourself before saving

quizzes.question: Where do you go to create a new email template in LeadProspectrr?

options.option_text: Contacts > Import
Marketing > Emails > Templates
Settings > Integrations
Dashboard > Reports

quizzes.explanation: Email templates are created in the Marketing section under Emails, then Templates.

quizzes.question: Why is it important to use clear template names?

options.option_text: It makes the email send faster
So you can easily find and identify the right template later
It improves email deliverability
It is required by LeadProspectrr

quizzes.explanation: Clear names like 'Welcome - New Lead' help you quickly find the right template when you need it, especially as your template library grows.

quizzes.question: What should you do before saving a new template?

options.option_text: Delete all other templates
Send yourself a test email to check how it looks
Share it on social media
Print a physical copy

quizzes.explanation: Always send yourself a test email to preview formatting, check links, and see how it appears on both desktop and mobile before saving.

title: Write Effective Email Content
learningGoal: Learn the simple structure for writing clear, effective emails that get results.

items.title: Subject Line
items.description: Tells them why to open the email. Keep it clear and specific.

items.title: First Line
items.description: Explains why they are receiving this email. Sets the context.

items.title: Main Message
items.description: Gives the useful information they need. Keep it concise.

items.title: Call to Action
items.description: Tells them exactly what to do next. One clear action.

items.title: Sign-Off
items.description: Keeps it personal and professional.

items.title: One email. One message. One action.
items.description: If your email tries to do too many things, people will do nothing. Focus on a single goal.

keyPoint: Write for your audience using words they understand. Keep sentences short and paragraphs to 2-3 sentences.

actionSteps.title: Choose one email to write
actionSteps.description: Pick a specific email you need to create from your plan

actionSteps.title: Write each section
actionSteps.description: Subject line, first line, main message, CTA, and sign-off

actionSteps.title: Check the one-action rule
actionSteps.description: Make sure you're only asking for one thing in this email

quizzes.question: What is the purpose of the subject line?

options.option_text: To tell the full story of the email
To tell them why they should open the email
To include all your contact information
To make the email look longer

quizzes.explanation: The subject line's job is to get the email opened. It should be clear, specific, and give the recipient a reason to open and read more.

quizzes.question: According to the golden rule, how many actions should one email contain?

options.option_text: As many as possible
Three to five actions
One clear action
It depends on the email length

quizzes.explanation: One email, one message, one action. Multiple calls-to-action confuse readers and reduce the chance they'll take any action at all.

quizzes.question: What should the first line of your email do?

options.option_text: Include your company history
List all your services
Explain why they are receiving this email and set the context
Ask for a sale immediately

quizzes.explanation: The first line sets context and reminds the recipient why they're getting this email, making them more likely to continue reading.

title: Add Personalization to Emails
learningGoal: Learn how to use personalization fields to make emails feel more human and relevant.

items.title: First name
items.description: Hi {{contact.first_name}}, makes the email feel personal

items.title: Business name
items.description: Reference their company or organization

items.title: Appointment time
items.description: Confirm scheduled meetings or calls

items.title: Calendar link
items.description: Personal booking links for each contact

items.title: Resource link
items.description: Specific guides or downloads they requested

items.title: Hi {{contact.first_name}},
items.description: Thanks for joining today's session. This small touch makes the email feel written just for them.

items.title: Always test personalization before sending
items.description: A broken personalization field like 'Hi {{contact.first_name}},' when the field is empty makes your email look careless and unprofessional

keyPoint: Personalization makes emails feel human, but broken personalization fields destroy credibility. Always test first.

actionSteps.title: Identify personalization opportunities
actionSteps.description: Look at your email and see where adding a name or detail would help

actionSteps.title: Add one personalization field
actionSteps.description: Start with first name - it's the most common and impactful

actionSteps.title: Send a test email
actionSteps.description: Verify the personalization renders correctly with real data

quizzes.question: What is the benefit of using personalization fields in emails?

options.option_text: It makes the email send faster
It makes the email feel more human and relevant to the recipient
It reduces the email file size
It automatically translates the email

quizzes.explanation: Personalization fields like first name make emails feel individually written, increasing engagement and response rates.

quizzes.question: What happens if a personalization field is broken or empty?

options.option_text: The email sends normally with no issues
The email looks careless and unprofessional
The email is automatically deleted
The recipient cannot open the email

quizzes.explanation: Broken personalization fields show the raw code (like '{{contact.first_name}}') or blank spaces, making your email look sloppy and automated rather than personal.

quizzes.question: Which personalization field is most commonly used and impactful?

options.option_text: IP address
First name
Browser type
Email domain

quizzes.explanation: First name is the most common and impactful personalization field. Starting an email with 'Hi Sarah,' feels much more personal than 'Hi there,' or 'Dear Customer,'

title: Create an Email Campaign
learningGoal: Learn how to create and send an email campaign to the right audience in LeadProspectrr.

items.title: 1. Go to Marketing > Email Campaigns
items.description: Navigate to the Campaigns section

items.title: 2. Create a new campaign
items.description: Click to start a new campaign

items.title: 3. Choose your email template
items.description: Select the template you created earlier

items.title: 4. Select the audience or smart list
items.description: Choose who should receive this email - not everyone, just the right group

items.title: 5. Confirm the contact list
items.description: Double-check you're sending to the right people

items.title: 6. Check sender name and email
items.description: Verify the from name and reply-to address

items.title: 7. Preview and send a test
items.description: See how it looks and test all links

items.title: 8. Schedule or send
items.description: Send immediately or schedule for later

items.title: 9. Review results
items.description: Check opens, clicks, and replies after sending

items.title: Send to the right group, not everyone
items.description: Do not send to everyone just because they are in the CRM. Send the right message to the right group.

keyPoint: Campaigns connect your template to your audience. Choose the right people and always test before sending.

actionSteps.title: Navigate to Marketing > Email Campaigns
actionSteps.description: Find the Campaigns section in LeadProspectrr

actionSteps.title: Create a new campaign
actionSteps.description: Start the campaign creation process

actionSteps.title: Select your template and audience
actionSteps.description: Choose the email template and the right smart list or audience

actionSteps.title: Send a test email
actionSteps.description: Always test before sending to your full list

quizzes.question: Where do you go to create an email campaign in LeadProspectrr?

options.option_text: Contacts > Import
Marketing > Email Campaigns
Settings > Users
Dashboard > Analytics

quizzes.explanation: Email campaigns are created in the Marketing section under Email Campaigns, separate from where you create templates.

quizzes.question: What should you do before sending a campaign to your full list?

options.option_text: Post about it on social media
Send a test email to yourself first
Delete your contact list
Wait for a holiday

quizzes.explanation: Always send yourself a test email to check formatting, links, personalization, and how it appears on different devices before sending to your full audience.

quizzes.question: Why shouldn't you send every campaign to your entire contact list?

options.option_text: It costs more money
Not everyone is interested in every message, which can lead to unsubscribes
The system won't allow it
It takes longer to send

quizzes.explanation: Sending irrelevant emails to your entire list leads to lower engagement and higher unsubscribe rates. Use smart lists to send the right message to the right people.

title: Review Before Sending
learningGoal: Learn the essential checklist to review before sending any email campaign.

items.title: Is the audience correct?
items.description: Double-check you're sending to the right people

items.title: Is the subject line clear?
items.description: Would you open this email?

items.title: Is the email too long?
items.description: Shorter emails get better response rates

items.title: Does the CTA make sense?
items.description: Is the next step clear and easy?

items.title: Do all links work?
items.description: Click every link to verify

items.title: Does it look good on mobile?
items.description: Most emails are opened on phones

items.title: Did I send myself a test?
items.description: Always test before the real send

items.title: Is the sender name correct?
items.description: Will recipients recognize who it's from?

items.title: Is the reply email correct?
items.description: Where do replies go?

keyPoint: Taking five minutes to review can save you from embarrassing mistakes and improve your results dramatically.

actionSteps.title: Print or save the checklist
actionSteps.description: Keep this checklist handy for every campaign

actionSteps.title: Review your current draft
actionSteps.description: Go through each item on the checklist

actionSteps.title: Fix any issues found
actionSteps.description: Make corrections before sending

quizzes.question: Why is it important to check if the email looks good on mobile?

options.option_text: Mobile emails are more expensive to send
Most emails are opened on mobile devices
Desktop email is being discontinued
Mobile emails send faster

quizzes.explanation: Over 60% of emails are opened on mobile devices. If your email doesn't look good on a phone, most of your audience will have a poor experience.

quizzes.question: What should you do if you find a broken link during your review?

options.option_text: Send it anyway - most people won't click
Fix the link before sending
Remove all links from the email
Add more links to compensate

quizzes.explanation: Broken links destroy credibility and waste the opportunity. Always fix broken links before sending - the call-to-action is the whole point of the email.

quizzes.question: How long should your review take?

options.option_text: At least one hour
Five minutes is enough to catch most issues
No review is needed if you use templates
Reviews should be done by a committee

quizzes.explanation: A quick five-minute review using a checklist can catch most major issues and save you from embarrassing mistakes. It's a small investment for much better results.

title: Understand Campaign Results
learningGoal: Learn what the basic campaign metrics mean and how to use them to improve future emails.

items.title: Sent
items.description: How many emails were successfully sent out

items.title: Opened
items.description: How many people opened the email - indicates subject line effectiveness

items.title: Clicked
items.description: How many clicked a link - shows CTA and content effectiveness

items.title: Replied
items.description: How many responded directly to the email

items.title: Bounced
items.description: Emails that couldn't be delivered - bad addresses

items.title: Unsubscribed
items.description: People who opted out - normal but watch for spikes

items.title: Low opens?
items.description: Your subject line may need work

items.title: Opens but no clicks?
items.description: Your CTA or offer may not be clear enough

items.title: Look for patterns
items.description: Don't judge one email too harshly - look at trends over time

keyPoint: Use results to improve, not to judge. One email is a data point - patterns over time show you what works.

actionSteps.title: Wait 24-48 hours after sending
actionSteps.description: Give people time to open and engage

actionSteps.title: Review your campaign results
actionSteps.description: Check opens, clicks, and other metrics in LeadProspectrr

actionSteps.title: Note one improvement
actionSteps.description: What will you do differently next time?

quizzes.question: What does a high open rate but low click rate indicate?

options.option_text: Your subject line is ineffective
Your call-to-action or offer isn't compelling enough
Your email is too short
You sent it at the wrong time of day

quizzes.explanation: If people open but don't click, your subject line worked (they opened) but your content or CTA didn't motivate action.

quizzes.question: What should you do if your open rate is low?

options.option_text: Send the same email again immediately
Work on improving your subject line
Add more links to the email
Send to more people

quizzes.explanation: Low open rates usually indicate the subject line isn't compelling enough. Test different subject lines to see what resonates with your audience.

quizzes.question: How should you interpret results from a single email campaign?

options.option_text: Judge it harshly if it doesn't perform perfectly
Use it as one data point and look for patterns over time
Delete the email and never send campaigns again
Immediately change your entire business strategy

quizzes.explanation: One email is a single data point. Look for patterns across multiple campaigns to understand what works for your specific audience.

title: Create Your Follow-Up Template
learningGoal: Apply everything you've learned to create a reusable follow-up email template for your business.

items.title: Scenario
items.description: Someone downloaded your free guide, attended your event, or spoke with you briefly but hasn't booked a call yet

items.title: Email Goal
items.description: Thank them, remind them why they connected, and invite them to take one next step

items.title: Template Name
items.description: Follow-Up - Book a Call

items.title: Choose one
items.description: Quick follow-up | Your next step | Thanks for connecting | Here's the next step we discussed

items.title: Hi {{contact.first_name}},
items.description: Thanks again for connecting. I wanted to follow up and share a simple next step. If you're still interested in [topic], we can schedule a short call and look at what would help most right now. [Calendar Link] Thanks, {{user.name}}

keyPoint: This template will become one of your most-used assets. Take time to get it right.

actionSteps.title: Create the email template
actionSteps.description: Go to Marketing > Emails > Templates and create your follow-up template

actionSteps.title: Name it clearly
actionSteps.description: Use 'Follow-Up - Book a Call' or similar descriptive name

actionSteps.title: Send yourself a test
actionSteps.description: Verify links work and personalization renders correctly

actionSteps.title: Save the template
actionSteps.description: Your follow-up template is now ready to use

quizzes.question: What is the primary goal of a follow-up email?

options.option_text: To tell your entire company history
To thank them, remind them why they connected, and invite one next step
To ask for multiple things at once
To send as many emails as possible

quizzes.explanation: Follow-up emails should be focused: thank the person, remind them of the context, and give them one clear next step to take.

quizzes.question: Why should you save follow-up emails as templates?

options.option_text: They are required by law
You will send this type of email repeatedly
Templates send automatically
They cost less to send

quizzes.explanation: Follow-up situations happen repeatedly in business. Having a template saves time and ensures consistency in your messaging.

quizzes.question: What should you always do before saving a follow-up template?

options.option_text: Share it on social media
Send yourself a test email to verify everything works
Ask your competitors to review it
Print a physical copy

quizzes.explanation: Always test your template by sending it to yourself. Check that links work, personalization renders correctly, and the formatting looks good.
